content_html:
Friday, 28 August 2020

Standards

The Internet Architecture Board (IAB) has published RFC8890, The Internet is for End Users, arguing that the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) should ground its decisions in what’s good for people who use the Internet, and that it should take positive steps to achieve that.

Why does this need to be said? Is it going too far? Who else could they favour, and why should you care? As author of the RFC and a member of the IAB that passed it, here are my thoughts.

How the Internet is made

The IETF plays a central role in the design and operation of the Internet. Formed in the 1980s by the engineers who created several of the Internet’s core technologies, it is the primary venue for documenting the technical design of the Internet, and has overseen development of protocols like TCP, IP, DNS and HTTP.

Companies, governments and other organisations don’t officially participate in the IETF; people only represent themselves. There isn’t even a concept of membership. Instead, decisions about specifications are made by ‘rough consensus’ — instead of formal voting, the IETF tries to find the best solution for each issue, based upon the ideas, comments and concerns brought to it.

‘Best' doesn't mean the choice that has the most companies supporting it; it’s the one that has the best technical arguments behind it. Working Group chairs measure that consensus; if someone thinks they got it wrong, they can appeal it through a chain of authorities selected for their experience.

Or, in the words of the unofficial IETF credo: ‘We reject kings, presidents and voting. We believe in rough consensus and running code.’

Technical or political? Both

Naturally, most IETF decisions are about technical details; what bytes should go where, how a server reacts to a client, and so on. Because of this, participants often tell themselves that their decisions aren't ever political; that any such concerns are on ‘layer 8’ — referring to the stack of seven abstractions commonly used for network protocols — and therefore nothing to be concerned about.

“[T]he running code that results from our process (when things work well) inevitably has an impact beyond technical considerations, because the underlying decisions afford some uses while discouraging others.”
— The Internet is for End Users

However, the barrier between the bits on the wire and political matters has turned out to be leaky, like most abstractions are. Sometimes the ability to send information (or the prevention of it) has real-world consequences that take power from some people and give it to others. Likewise with the ability to see what other people are saying, and to control the format in which they speak.

So, in a world that is increasingly intertwined with the Internet, it’s becoming more difficult to maintain the position that the design of Internet protocols doesn't have a political dimension. All decisions have the possibility of bias; of advantaging or disadvantaging different parties.

For example, the recent standardisation of DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) pitted advocates for dissidents and protestors against network operators who use DNS for centralised network management, and child safety advocates who promote DNS-based filtering solutions. If the IETF were to only decide upon technical merit, how would it balance these interests?

Another example is the Encrypted Client Hello proposal, which closes a loophole that shares the identity of HTTPS sites you visit with anyone listening. China has reportedly started blocking connections that use it, so in a purely technical sense, it will not work well because some networks block it. Should the IETF stop working on it?

Yet another example: how should the IETF handle a proposal to allow networks to decrypt or intermediate HTTPS connections? Is that OK if it’s merely technically sound? What if the user agrees to it, and what does ‘consent’ mean? Many such proposals have been made, but not approved. Why?

If the IETF’s decisions affect the design of the Internet, and the Internet is political, the IETF’s decisions are sometimes political too. However, its decision-making processes presume that there is a technically correct answer to each problem. When that decision affects people and power in the actual world, rough consensus and running code are insufficient.

Over the years, these questions have become increasingly urgent, because it isn’t viable to make decisions that have political outcomes but explain them using only technical arguments. That endangers the legitimacy of the IETF’s decisions, because they can be viewed as arbitrary, especially by those on the losing side.

Many rule-making systems — whether they be courts, legislatures or standards bodies — establish legitimacy by taking a principled approach. A community that agrees to principles that are informed by shared values can use them to navigate hard decisions. It's reasonable, then, to consider the principles that the IETF uses to guide development of the Internet.

The Internet’s principles

The Internet as we know it is a product of the times in which it grew up. The rule of law and liberal values of equality, reason, liberty, rights, and property were all dominant in the political landscape of post-war America and Europe, where most early Internet development took place.

“The IETF community wants the Internet to succeed because we believe that the existence of the Internet, and its influence on economics, communication, and education, will help us to build a better human society.”
— A Mission Statement
for the IETF

The Internet has implicitly embedded those values. You don’t need a license (or even to disclose your identity) to use it, and its technical underpinnings make it difficult to impose that requirement. Anyone can publish, and as a result it takes significant effort for a government to restrict the rights to speech and free assembly on it — again due in part to the way it is designed. There isn’t any central authority that decides what networks can or can’t attach to the Internet. You can create a new Internet application without getting permission first (just like Tim Berners-Lee did so long ago when he created the Web). Such openness is often cited as critical to the Internet’s success.

However, implicit values can drift, as new people get involved in the work, and as new challenges are faced. This is especially true when the resulting decisions can have profound effects on both profits and societies. So, over the years, the IETF community has made progress in documenting explicit principles that can guide decision-making.

For example, RFC 7258 Pervasive Monitoring Is an Attack established IETF consensus that it’s bad for the Internet to allow widespread, covert monitoring, and that therefore the IETF would design its protocols to mitigate this risk —a technical argument with both political motivation and ramifications.

Likewise, RFC 6973 documents Privacy Considerations for Internet Protocols, and RFC 8752 reports on an IAB workshop that explored the power dynamics between news publishers and large online platforms.

Or, consider the end-to-end principle, which states that features for applications should reside in the end nodes (for example, your computer or phone) rather than in the network.

The IETF community will (I hope) continue to document and explore such principles, informed by shared values. RFC8890 makes a small contribution to this, by asking the IETF community to favour end users of the Internet — in other words, actual people — over other stakeholders that ask for their needs to be met, when there’s a conflict.

We can’t just stick to the technology

If the IETF didn’t have any underlying principles, it would just focus on technology. A few detractors of The Internet is for End Users have said that’s exactly what it should do. That means that it would publish any proposal, no matter what its effects, provided that it was technically sufficient.

Some standards bodies already operate in that fashion; as long as you can get a few people (or more often, companies) together and agree on something, you can get it published. The IETF does not; it often declines to adopt proposals.

“When the IETF takes ownership of a protocol or function, it accepts the responsibility for all aspects of the protocol, even though some aspects may rarely or never be seen on the Internet.”
— A Mission Statement
for the IETF

That ability to refuse is meaningful to many people inside and outside the organisation; the IETF standardising something implies that it is good for the Internet, and has been reviewed not only for technical suitability but also adherence to the principles that inform the Internet’s design. In other words, the IETF is a quality filter; if a specification achieves consensus there, it gets deployed more broadly and easily (although it’s not a guarantee of success by any means) because people know it’s had that scrutiny.

Abdicating that role just to avoid thinking about and applying principles would not be good for the Internet. While it might gain a few participants eager to take advantage, it would lose many — including many of those who are still invested in the Internet as a force for good in the world.

Doing so would also affect the legitimacy of the IETF’s role in Internet governance in many eyes. There is a long history of scientists and engineers being concerned with how their work affects the world, and its potential for misuse. The IETF has continued this tradition, and should do so openly.

Getting comfortable with the IETF’s power

If the IETF is making decisions based upon what it thinks is good for users, is it setting itself up as being some sort of governing body, taking power away from governments and other institutions? Isn’t it dangerous to leave such important matters in the hands of the geeks who show up, and who don’t have any democratic legitimacy?

First of all, a reality check. IETF decisions are only about documents; they don’t control the Internet. Other parties like equipment and software vendors, end users, platform and network operators and ultimately governments have a lot more say in what actually happens on the Internet from day to day.

What the IETF has is a proven ability to design protocols that work at scale, the ability to steer a proposal to align with its principles, and a reputation that gives its documents a certain amount of gravitas. These draw those parties to the IETF as a venue for standardisation, and their power flows into the specifications it endorses — especially when a protocol has momentum, like HTTP or IP. It doesn’t work the other way around; if an IETF standard doesn’t catch on with implementers and users, it gets ignored (and many have).

The Internet is for End Users argues that this soft power should be explicitly acknowledged, so that participants are more conscious of the real-world ramifications of their decisions.

DNS over HTTPS is an interesting case study. It got the IETF mentioned in the UK Parliament by Baroness Thornton, a child safety advocate concerned about DoH’s use to bypass DNS-based controls mandated by UK law:

’[T]here is a fundamental and very concerning lack of accountability when obscure technical groups, peopled largely by the employees of the big internet companies, take decisions that have major public policy implications with enormous consequences for all of us…’

However, DoH was designed, contributed and ultimately deployed by participants from Web browsers, not the IETF, who cannot stop vendors from deploying a protocol it doesn’t approve of (as is often said, ‘there are no standards police.’). The IETF’s contribution was putting the specification through its process to assess its technical suitability and adherence to established principles.

Did the IETF create a better internet when it approved DoH? There’s a lot of disagreement about that, but what has upset many is that DoH was a surprise — the IETF standardised it without consulting some who it was likely to affect. Here, the IETF could have done better. The Internet is for End Users argues that such consultation is important, to assure that the people writing and reviewing the protocols understand how they will be used, and how they will impact users.

In the case of DoH, better communication between the technical community (not just big tech companies) and policymakers would clarified that relying on DNS to impose filtering was a bad assumption, in light of the principles underlying the design of the Internet.

“From its inception, the Internet has been, and is expected to remain, an evolving system whose participants regularly factor new requirements and technology into its design and implementation. Users of the Internet and providers of the equipment, software, and services that support it should anticipate and embrace this evolution as a major tenet of Internet philosophy.”
— The Internet Standards Process

However, that consultation does not translate to giving other parties a veto over Internet protocols. The UK Government or any other external authority should not be able to stop the IETF from creating a particular standard, or to hold it directly accountable; that would be a radical break from how the Internet has been developed for over thirty years. Because of the global nature of the Internet, it wouldn’t be possible to pursue a bilateral or regional style of governance; decisions would have to be sanctioned by every government where the Internet operates. That’s difficult to achieve even for vague statements of shared goals; doing it for the details of network protocols is impractical.

Who, then, is the IETF accountable to? Besides the internal rules which assure that the standards process runs in a way that’s accountable to the technical community, ultimately the IETF is accountable to the Internet; if it strays too far from what vendors, networks, users, and governments want to do, it will lose relevance. As with any platform, the Internet is a beneficiary of the network effect, and if the IETF leads it in a direction that’s unacceptable in too many places, the Internet might fragment into several networks — a risk currently on many people’s minds.

Finding what’s best for end users

There are also bound to be situations where what is best for end users is not obvious. Some will claim that giving other parties power — to filter, to monitor, to block — is in the interest of end users. How will the IETF make those decisions?

Unsurprisingly, this has already happened; it refused to standardise wiretapping technology, for example. In doing so, it applied technical reasoning informed by principles and the global nature of the Internet; designing Internet standards to suit the laws of one or a few countries isn’t appropriate.

That is echoed by The Internet is for End Users, which says:

[W]hen a decision improves the Internet for end users in one jurisdiction, but at the cost of potential harm to others elsewhere, that is not a good tradeoff. As such, we effectively design the Internet for the pessimal environment.

Even with careful thought, technical acumen and broad consultation, the IETF is bound to get some decisions wrong. That’s OK. RFC stands for Request for Comments, and in that spirit, sometimes the comments — evidenced by adoption and deployment as well — tell us to revise our specifications. That spirit of humility is still very much alive in the IETF community.

Next steps

The Internet has been with us for almost 40 years and has contributed to profound changes in society. It currently faces serious challenges — issues that require input from policymakers, civil society, ordinary citizens, businesses and technologists.

It’s past time for technologists to both become more involved in discussions about how to meet those challenges, and to consider broader views of how the technology they create fits into society. Without good communication, policymakers are prone to making rules that doesn’t work with the technology, and technologists are prone to creating technology naïve to its policy implications.

So at its heart, The Internet is for End Users is a call for IETF participants to stop pretending that they can ignore the non-technical consequences of their decisions, a call for broader consultation when making them, and one for continued focus on the end user. Ultimately, end user impact is as least as important as the technical considerations of a proposal, and judging that impact requires a more serious effort to understand and incorporate other non-technical views.

The Internet is for End Users is an IAB document; it doesn't have IETF consensus. As such, it doesn’t bind IETF decisions, but it is considered persuasive because the IAB has a mandate to consider issues affecting the Internet architecture.

On its own, then, it has limited effect. I view it as a small contribution to a larger body of principled thought that can help inform decisions about the evolution of the Internet. It’s up to all of us to apply those principles and develop them further.

Thanks to Martin Thomson and Eric Rescorla for reviewing this article.

sentences.en: The IETF plays a central role in the design and operation of the Internet.
sentences.zh: IETF 在互联网的设计和运营中发挥着核心作用。

sentences.en: Formed in the 1980s by the engineers who created several of the Internet’s core technologies, it is the primary venue for documenting the technical design of the Internet, and has overseen development of protocols like TCP, IP, DNS and HTTP.
sentences.zh: 它由创建了多项互联网核心技术的工程师于 20 世纪 80 年代成立，是记录互联网技术设计的主要场所，并监督 TCP、IP、DNS 和 HTTP 等协议的开发。

blocks.html_en: Companies, governments and other organisations don’t officially participate in the IETF; people only represent themselves. There isn’t even a concept of membership. Instead, decisions about specifications are made by ‘rough consensus’ — instead of formal voting, the IETF tries to find the best solution for each issue, based upon the ideas, comments and concerns brought to it.

sentences.en: Companies, governments and other organisations don’t officially participate in the IETF; people only represent themselves.
sentences.zh: 公司、政府和其他组织并未正式参与 IETF；人们只代表他们自己。

sentences.en: There isn’t even a concept of membership.
sentences.zh: 甚至没有会员资格的概念。

sentences.en: Instead, decisions about specifications are made by ‘rough consensus’ — instead of formal voting, the IETF tries to find the best solution for each issue, based upon the ideas, comments and concerns brought to it.
sentences.zh: 相反，有关规范的决定是通过“粗略共识”做出的——IETF 试图根据提出的想法、评论和担忧找到每个问题的最佳解决方案，而不是正式投票。

blocks.html_en: ‘Best' doesn't mean the choice that has the most companies supporting it; it’s the one that has the best technical arguments behind it. Working Group chairs measure that consensus; if someone thinks they got it wrong, they can appeal it through a chain of authorities selected for their experience.

sentences.en: ‘Best' doesn't mean the choice that has the most companies supporting it; it’s the one that has the best technical arguments behind it.
sentences.zh: “最好”并不意味着得到最多公司支持的选择；它背后有最好的技术论证。

sentences.en: Working Group chairs measure that consensus; if someone thinks they got it wrong, they can appeal it through a chain of authorities selected for their experience.
sentences.zh: 工作组主席衡量这一共识；如果有人认为自己错了，他们可以通过一系列根据他们的经验选择的权威机构提出上诉。

blocks.html_en: Or, in the words of the unofficial IETF credo: ‘We reject kings, presidents and voting. We believe in rough consensus and running code.’

sentences.en: Or, in the words of the unofficial IETF credo: ‘We reject kings, presidents and voting.
sentences.zh: 或者，用非官方 IETF 信条的话来说：“我们拒绝国王、总统和投票。”

sentences.en: We believe in rough consensus and running code.’
sentences.zh: 我们相信粗略的共识和运行代码。”

blocks.html_en: Technical or political? Both

sentences.en: Technical or political?
sentences.zh: 技术还是政治？

sentences.en: Both
sentences.zh: 两个都

blocks.html_en: Naturally, most IETF decisions are about technical details; what bytes should go where, how a server reacts to a client, and so on. Because of this, participants often tell themselves that their decisions aren't ever political; that any such concerns are on ‘layer 8’ — referring to the stack of seven abstractions commonly used for network protocols — and therefore nothing to be concerned about.

sentences.en: Naturally, most IETF decisions are about technical details; what bytes should go where, how a server reacts to a client, and so on.
sentences.zh: 当然，大多数 IETF 决策都是关于技术细节的；哪些字节应该放在哪里，服务器如何对客户端做出反应，等等。

sentences.en: Because of this, participants often tell themselves that their decisions aren't ever political; that any such concerns are on ‘layer 8’ — referring to the stack of seven abstractions commonly used for network protocols — and therefore nothing to be concerned about.
sentences.zh: 正因为如此，参与者经常告诉自己，他们的决定从来都不是政治性的；他们的决定与政治无关。任何此类问题都发生在“第 8 层”上——指的是网络协议常用的七个抽象堆栈——因此无需担心。

blocks.html_en:
“[T]he running code that results from our process (when things work well) inevitably has an impact beyond technical considerations, because the underlying decisions afford some uses while discouraging others.”
— The Internet is for End Users

sentences.en: “[T]he running code that results from our process (when things work well) inevitably has an impact beyond technical considerations, because the underlying decisions afford some uses while discouraging others.” — The Internet is for End Users
sentences.zh: “运行由我们的流程产生的代码（当事情运行良好时）不可避免地会产生超出技术考虑的影响，因为基本决策提供了一些用途，同时阻碍了其他用途。” — 互联网是为最终用户服务的

blocks.html_en: However, the barrier between the bits on the wire and political matters has turned out to be leaky, like most abstractions are. Sometimes the ability to send information (or the prevention of it) has real-world consequences that take power from some people and give it to others. Likewise with the ability to see what other people are saying, and to control the format in which they speak.

sentences.en: However, the barrier between the bits on the wire and political matters has turned out to be leaky, like most abstractions are.
sentences.zh: 然而，就像大多数抽象概念一样，网络上的比特和政治事务之间的障碍已经被证明是有漏洞的。

sentences.en: Sometimes the ability to send information (or the prevention of it) has real-world consequences that take power from some people and give it to others.
sentences.zh: 有时，发送信息（或阻止信息）的能力会产生现实世界的后果，即夺取某些人的权力并将其交给其他人。

sentences.en: Likewise with the ability to see what other people are saying, and to control the format in which they speak.
sentences.zh: 同样，能够看到其他人在说什么，并控制他们说话的格式。

blocks.html_en: So, in a world that is increasingly intertwined with the Internet, it’s becoming more difficult to maintain the position that the design of Internet protocols doesn't have a political dimension. All decisions have the possibility of bias; of advantaging or disadvantaging different parties.

sentences.en: So, in a world that is increasingly intertwined with the Internet, it’s becoming more difficult to maintain the position that the design of Internet protocols doesn't have a political dimension.
sentences.zh: 因此，在一个与互联网日益交织在一起的世界中，维持互联网协议的设计不具有政治维度的立场变得越来越困难。

sentences.en: All decisions have the possibility of bias; of advantaging or disadvantaging different parties.
sentences.zh: 所有的决定都可能存在偏见；对不同各方有利或不利的情况。

blocks.html_en: For example, the recent standardisation of DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) pitted advocates for dissidents and protestors against network operators who use DNS for centralised network management, and child safety advocates who promote DNS-based filtering solutions. If the IETF were to only decide upon technical merit, how would it balance these interests?

sentences.en: For example, the recent standardisation of DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) pitted advocates for dissidents and protestors against network operators who use DNS for centralised network management, and child safety advocates who promote DNS-based filtering solutions.
sentences.zh: 例如，最近的 DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) 标准化让持不同政见者和抗议者的拥护者与使用 DNS 进行集中式网络管理的网络运营商以及推广基于 DNS 的过滤解决方案的儿童安全倡导者展开了对立。

sentences.en: If the IETF were to only decide upon technical merit, how would it balance these interests?
sentences.zh: 如果 IETF 仅根据技术优点做出决定，它将如何平衡这些利益？

blocks.html_en: Another example is the Encrypted Client Hello proposal, which closes a loophole that shares the identity of HTTPS sites you visit with anyone listening. China has reportedly started blocking connections that use it, so in a purely technical sense, it will not work well because some networks block it. Should the IETF stop working on it?

sentences.en: Another example is the Encrypted Client Hello proposal, which closes a loophole that shares the identity of HTTPS sites you visit with anyone listening.
sentences.zh: 另一个例子是 Encrypted Client Hello 提案，它弥补了与任何监听者共享您访问的 HTTPS 站点身份的漏洞。

sentences.en: China has reportedly started blocking connections that use it, so in a purely technical sense, it will not work well because some networks block it.
sentences.zh: 据报道，中国已开始阻止使用它的连接，因此从纯粹的技术意义上来说，它不会很好地工作，因为某些网络会阻止它。

sentences.en: Should the IETF stop working on it?
sentences.zh: IETF 应该停止这方面的工作吗？

blocks.html_en: Yet another example: how should the IETF handle a proposal to allow networks to decrypt or intermediate HTTPS connections? Is that OK if it’s merely technically sound? What if the user agrees to it, and what does ‘consent’ mean? Many such proposals have been made, but not approved. Why?

sentences.en: Yet another example: how should the IETF handle a proposal to allow networks to decrypt or intermediate HTTPS connections?
sentences.zh: 另一个例子：IETF 应如何处理允许网络解密或中间 HTTPS 连接的提案？

sentences.en: Is that OK if it’s merely technically sound?
sentences.zh: 如果仅仅是技术上合理的话可以吗？

sentences.en: What if the user agrees to it, and what does ‘consent’ mean?
sentences.zh: 如果用户同意怎么办？“同意”是什么意思？

sentences.en: Many such proposals have been made, but not approved.
sentences.zh: 已经提出了许多这样的建议，但没有获得批准。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

blocks.html_en: If the IETF’s decisions affect the design of the Internet, and the Internet is political, the IETF’s decisions are sometimes political too. However, its decision-making processes presume that there is a technically correct answer to each problem. When that decision affects people and power in the actual world, rough consensus and running code are insufficient.

sentences.en: If the IETF’s decisions affect the design of the Internet, and the Internet is political, the IETF’s decisions are sometimes political too.
sentences.zh: 如果 IETF 的决定影响互联网的设计，而互联网是政治性的，那么 IETF 的决定有时也是政治性的。

sentences.en: However, its decision-making processes presume that there is a technically correct answer to each problem.
sentences.zh: 然而，其决策过程假定每个问题都有技术上正确的答案。

sentences.en: When that decision affects people and power in the actual world, rough consensus and running code are insufficient.
sentences.zh: 当这个决定影响现实世界中的人和权力时，粗略的共识和运行代码是不够的。

blocks.html_en: Over the years, these questions have become increasingly urgent, because it isn’t viable to make decisions that have political outcomes but explain them using only technical arguments. That endangers the legitimacy of the IETF’s decisions, because they can be viewed as arbitrary, especially by those on the losing side.

sentences.en: Over the years, these questions have become increasingly urgent, because it isn’t viable to make decisions that have political outcomes but explain them using only technical arguments.
sentences.zh: 多年来，这些问题变得越来越紧迫，因为做出具有政治结果的决策但仅使用技术论证来解释它们是不可行的。

sentences.en: That endangers the legitimacy of the IETF’s decisions, because they can be viewed as arbitrary, especially by those on the losing side.
sentences.zh: 这危及了 IETF 决策的合法性，因为这些决策可能被视为任意的，尤其是对于那些失败的一方。

blocks.html_en: Many rule-making systems — whether they be courts, legislatures or standards bodies — establish legitimacy by taking a principled approach. A community that agrees to principles that are informed by shared values can use them to navigate hard decisions. It's reasonable, then, to consider the principles that the IETF uses to guide development of the Internet.

sentences.en: Many rule-making systems — whether they be courts, legislatures or standards bodies — establish legitimacy by taking a principled approach.
sentences.zh: 许多规则制定系统——无论是法院、立法机构还是标准机构——通过采取有原则的方法来建立合法性。

sentences.en: A community that agrees to principles that are informed by shared values can use them to navigate hard decisions.
sentences.zh: 同意基于共同价值观的原则的社区可以利用这些原则来做出艰难的决策。

sentences.en: It's reasonable, then, to consider the principles that the IETF uses to guide development of the Internet.
sentences.zh: 因此，考虑 IETF 用来指导互联网发展的原则是合理的。

blocks.html_en: The Internet’s principles

sentences.en: The Internet’s principles
sentences.zh: 互联网的原理

blocks.html_en: The Internet as we know it is a product of the times in which it grew up. The rule of law and liberal values of equality, reason, liberty, rights, and property were all dominant in the political landscape of post-war America and Europe, where most early Internet development took place.

sentences.en: The Internet as we know it is a product of the times in which it grew up.
sentences.zh: 我们所知道的互联网是它成长的时代的产物。

sentences.en: The rule of law and liberal values of equality, reason, liberty, rights, and property were all dominant in the political landscape of post-war America and Europe, where most early Internet development took place.
sentences.zh: 法治和平等、理性、自由、权利和财产等自由主义价值观在战后美国和欧洲的政治格局中占据主导地位，而最早期的互联网发展就发生在这些地方。

blocks.html_en:
“The IETF community wants the Internet to succeed because we believe that the existence of the Internet, and its influence on economics, communication, and education, will help us to build a better human society.”
— A Mission Statement
for the IETF

sentences.en: “The IETF community wants the Internet to succeed because we believe that the existence of the Internet, and its influence on economics, communication, and education, will help us to build a better human society.” — A Mission Statement for the IETF
sentences.zh: “IETF 社区希望互联网取得成功，因为我们相信互联网的存在及其对经济、通信和教育的影响将帮助我们建设一个更美好的人类社会。” — IETF 的使命宣言

blocks.html_en: The Internet has implicitly embedded those values. You don’t need a license (or even to disclose your identity) to use it, and its technical underpinnings make it difficult to impose that requirement. Anyone can publish, and as a result it takes significant effort for a government to restrict the rights to speech and free assembly on it — again due in part to the way it is designed. There isn’t any central authority that decides what networks can or can’t attach to the Internet. You can create a new Internet application without getting permission first (just like Tim Berners-Lee did so long ago when he created the Web). Such openness is often cited as critical to the Internet’s success.

sentences.en: The Internet has implicitly embedded those values.
sentences.zh: 互联网已经隐含地嵌入了这些价值观。

sentences.en: You don’t need a license (or even to disclose your identity) to use it, and its technical underpinnings make it difficult to impose that requirement.
sentences.zh: 您不需要许可证（甚至不需要披露您的身份）即可使用它，并且其技术基础使得很难强制执行该要求。

sentences.en: Anyone can publish, and as a result it takes significant effort for a government to restrict the rights to speech and free assembly on it — again due in part to the way it is designed.
sentences.zh: 任何人都可以发表文章，因此政府需要付出巨大的努力来限制言论和自由集会的权利——这在一定程度上也是由于它的设计方式。

sentences.en: There isn’t any central authority that decides what networks can or can’t attach to the Internet.
sentences.zh: 没有任何中央机构来决定哪些网络可以或不能连接到互联网。

sentences.en: You can create a new Internet application without getting permission first (just like Tim Berners-Lee did so long ago when he created the Web).
sentences.zh: 您无需事先获得许可即可创建新的 Internet 应用程序（就像蒂姆·伯纳斯·李很久以前创建 Web 时所做的那样）。

sentences.en: Such openness is often cited as critical to the Internet’s success.
sentences.zh: 这种开放性常常被认为对互联网的成功至关重要。

blocks.html_en: However, implicit values can drift, as new people get involved in the work, and as new challenges are faced. This is especially true when the resulting decisions can have profound effects on both profits and societies. So, over the years, the IETF community has made progress in documenting explicit principles that can guide decision-making.

sentences.en: However, implicit values can drift, as new people get involved in the work, and as new challenges are faced.
sentences.zh: 然而，随着新人参与工作并面临新挑战，隐含的价值观可能会发生变化。

sentences.en: This is especially true when the resulting decisions can have profound effects on both profits and societies.
sentences.zh: 当最终的决策对利润和社会产生深远影响时尤其如此。

sentences.en: So, over the years, the IETF community has made progress in documenting explicit principles that can guide decision-making.
sentences.zh: 因此，多年来，IETF 社区在记录可指导决策的明确原则方面取得了进展。

blocks.html_en: For example, RFC 7258 Pervasive Monitoring Is an Attack established IETF consensus that it’s bad for the Internet to allow widespread, covert monitoring, and that therefore the IETF would design its protocols to mitigate this risk —a technical argument with both political motivation and ramifications.

sentences.en: For example, RFC 7258 Pervasive Monitoring Is an Attack established IETF consensus that it’s bad for the Internet to allow widespread, covert monitoring, and that therefore the IETF would design its protocols to mitigate this risk —a technical argument with both political motivation and ramifications.
sentences.zh: 例如，RFC 7258 普遍监控是一种攻击建立了 IETF 共识，即允许广泛、隐蔽的监控对互联网不利，因此 IETF 将设计其协议来减轻这种风险——这是一个具有政治动机和后果的技术论点。

blocks.html_en: Likewise, RFC 6973 documents Privacy Considerations for Internet Protocols, and RFC 8752 reports on an IAB workshop that explored the power dynamics between news publishers and large online platforms.

sentences.en: Likewise, RFC 6973 documents Privacy Considerations for Internet Protocols, and RFC 8752 reports on an IAB workshop that explored the power dynamics between news publishers and large online platforms.
sentences.zh: 同样，RFC 6973 记录了互联网协议的隐私注意事项，RFC 8752 报告了 IAB 研讨会，该研讨会探讨了新闻出版商与大型在线平台之间的权力动态。

blocks.html_en: Or, consider the end-to-end principle, which states that features for applications should reside in the end nodes (for example, your computer or phone) rather than in the network.

sentences.en: Or, consider the end-to-end principle, which states that features for applications should reside in the end nodes (for example, your computer or phone) rather than in the network.
sentences.zh: 或者，考虑端到端原则，该原则规定应用程序的功能应驻留在终端节点（例如，您的计算机或电话）而不是网络中。

blocks.html_en: The IETF community will (I hope) continue to document and explore such principles, informed by shared values. RFC8890 makes a small contribution to this, by asking the IETF community to favour end users of the Internet — in other words, actual people — over other stakeholders that ask for their needs to be met, when there’s a conflict.

sentences.en: The IETF community will (I hope) continue to document and explore such principles, informed by shared values.
sentences.zh: IETF 社区将（我希望）继续以共同价值观为基础记录和探索这些原则。

sentences.en: RFC8890 makes a small contribution to this, by asking the IETF community to favour end users of the Internet — in other words, actual people — over other stakeholders that ask for their needs to be met, when there’s a conflict.
sentences.zh: RFC8890 对此做出了小小的贡献，要求 IETF 社区在发生冲突时支持互联网的最终用户（换句话说，实际的人），而不是要求满足其需求的其他利益相关者。

blocks.html_en: We can’t just stick to the technology

sentences.en: We can’t just stick to the technology
sentences.zh: 我们不能只拘泥于技术

blocks.html_en: If the IETF didn’t have any underlying principles, it would just focus on technology. A few detractors of The Internet is for End Users have said that’s exactly what it should do. That means that it would publish any proposal, no matter what its effects, provided that it was technically sufficient.

sentences.en: If the IETF didn’t have any underlying principles, it would just focus on technology.
sentences.zh: 如果 IETF 没有任何基本原则，它就会只关注技术。

sentences.en: A few detractors of The Internet is for End Users have said that’s exactly what it should do.
sentences.zh: 互联网是为最终用户服务的一些批评者表示，这正是它应该做的。

sentences.en: That means that it would publish any proposal, no matter what its effects, provided that it was technically sufficient.
sentences.zh: 这意味着只要技术上足够，它就会发布任何提案，无论其效果如何。

blocks.html_en: Some standards bodies already operate in that fashion; as long as you can get a few people (or more often, companies) together and agree on something, you can get it published. The IETF does not; it often declines to adopt proposals.

sentences.en: Some standards bodies already operate in that fashion; as long as you can get a few people (or more often, companies) together and agree on something, you can get it published.
sentences.zh: 一些标准机构已经以这种方式运作；只要你能让几个人（或更常见的是公司）聚集在一起并就某件事达成一致，你就可以将其发布。

sentences.en: The IETF does not; it often declines to adopt proposals.
sentences.zh: IETF 没有；它经常拒绝采纳建议。

blocks.html_en:
“When the IETF takes ownership of a protocol or function, it accepts the responsibility for all aspects of the protocol, even though some aspects may rarely or never be seen on the Internet.”
— A Mission Statement
for the IETF

sentences.en: “When the IETF takes ownership of a protocol or function, it accepts the responsibility for all aspects of the protocol, even though some aspects may rarely or never be seen on the Internet.” — A Mission Statement for the IETF
sentences.zh: “当 IETF 拥有某个协议或功能时，它就对该协议的所有方面承担责任，即使某些方面可能很少或永远不会在互联网上看到。” — IETF 的使命宣言

blocks.html_en: That ability to refuse is meaningful to many people inside and outside the organisation; the IETF standardising something implies that it is good for the Internet, and has been reviewed not only for technical suitability but also adherence to the principles that inform the Internet’s design. In other words, the IETF is a quality filter; if a specification achieves consensus there, it gets deployed more broadly and easily (although it’s not a guarantee of success by any means) because people know it’s had that scrutiny.

sentences.en: That ability to refuse is meaningful to many people inside and outside the organisation; the IETF standardising something implies that it is good for the Internet, and has been reviewed not only for technical suitability but also adherence to the principles that inform the Internet’s design.
sentences.zh: 这种拒绝的能力对于组织内外的许多人来说都是有意义的。 IETF 标准化某些东西意味着它对互联网有利，并且不仅对技术适用性进行了审查，而且还对互联网设计原则的遵守进行了审查。

sentences.en: In other words, the IETF is a quality filter; if a specification achieves consensus there, it gets deployed more broadly and easily (although it’s not a guarantee of success by any means) because people know it’s had that scrutiny.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，IETF 是一个质量过滤器；如果某个规范在那里达成共识，它就会得到更广泛、更容易的部署（尽管无论如何这并不能保证成功），因为人们知道它已经过审查。

blocks.html_en: Abdicating that role just to avoid thinking about and applying principles would not be good for the Internet. While it might gain a few participants eager to take advantage, it would lose many — including many of those who are still invested in the Internet as a force for good in the world.

sentences.en: Abdicating that role just to avoid thinking about and applying principles would not be good for the Internet.
sentences.zh: 仅仅为了避免思考和应用原则而放弃这一角色对于互联网来说并不好。

sentences.en: While it might gain a few participants eager to take advantage, it would lose many — including many of those who are still invested in the Internet as a force for good in the world.
sentences.zh: 虽然它可能会赢得一些渴望利用的参与者，但它也会失去很多人——包括许多仍然投资于互联网作为世界正义力量的人。

blocks.html_en: Doing so would also affect the legitimacy of the IETF’s role in Internet governance in many eyes. There is a long history of scientists and engineers being concerned with how their work affects the world, and its potential for misuse. The IETF has continued this tradition, and should do so openly.

sentences.en: Doing so would also affect the legitimacy of the IETF’s role in Internet governance in many eyes.
sentences.zh: 在许多人看来，这样做还会影响 IETF 在互联网治理中的作用的合法性。

sentences.en: There is a long history of scientists and engineers being concerned with how their work affects the world, and its potential for misuse.
sentences.zh: 科学家和工程师长期以来一直关注他们的工作如何影响世界及其被滥用的可能性。

sentences.en: The IETF has continued this tradition, and should do so openly.
sentences.zh: IETF 延续了这一传统，并且应该公开这样做。

blocks.html_en: Getting comfortable with the IETF’s power

sentences.en: Getting comfortable with the IETF’s power
sentences.zh: 熟悉 IETF 的力量

blocks.html_en: If the IETF is making decisions based upon what it thinks is good for users, is it setting itself up as being some sort of governing body, taking power away from governments and other institutions? Isn’t it dangerous to leave such important matters in the hands of the geeks who show up, and who don’t have any democratic legitimacy?

sentences.en: If the IETF is making decisions based upon what it thinks is good for users, is it setting itself up as being some sort of governing body, taking power away from governments and other institutions?
sentences.zh: 如果 IETF 是根据它认为对用户有利的方式做出决策，那么它是否会将自己定位为某种管理机构，从而从政府和其他机构手中夺取权力？

sentences.en: Isn’t it dangerous to leave such important matters in the hands of the geeks who show up, and who don’t have any democratic legitimacy?
sentences.zh: 把如此重要的事情交给那些出现的、没有任何民主合法性的极客手中，不是很危险吗？

blocks.html_en: First of all, a reality check. IETF decisions are only about documents; they don’t control the Internet. Other parties like equipment and software vendors, end users, platform and network operators and ultimately governments have a lot more say in what actually happens on the Internet from day to day.

sentences.en: First of all, a reality check.
sentences.zh: 首先，现实检查。

sentences.en: IETF decisions are only about documents; they don’t control the Internet.
sentences.zh: IETF 的决定仅与文件有关；他们不控制互联网。

sentences.en: Other parties like equipment and software vendors, end users, platform and network operators and ultimately governments have a lot more say in what actually happens on the Internet from day to day.
sentences.zh: 设备和软件供应商、最终用户、平台和网络运营商以及最终政府等其他各方对于互联网上每天实际发生的事情拥有更多发言权。

blocks.html_en: What the IETF has is a proven ability to design protocols that work at scale, the ability to steer a proposal to align with its principles, and a reputation that gives its documents a certain amount of gravitas. These draw those parties to the IETF as a venue for standardisation, and their power flows into the specifications it endorses — especially when a protocol has momentum, like HTTP or IP. It doesn’t work the other way around; if an IETF standard doesn’t catch on with implementers and users, it gets ignored (and many have).

sentences.en: What the IETF has is a proven ability to design protocols that work at scale, the ability to steer a proposal to align with its principles, and a reputation that gives its documents a certain amount of gravitas.
sentences.zh: IETF 拥有设计大规模协议的能力、引导提案与其原则保持一致的能力，以及赋予其文档一定严肃性的声誉。

sentences.en: These draw those parties to the IETF as a venue for standardisation, and their power flows into the specifications it endorses — especially when a protocol has momentum, like HTTP or IP.
sentences.zh: 这些吸引了这些各方加入 IETF 作为标准化场所，他们的力量流向了它所认可的规范——尤其是当协议具有势头时，例如 HTTP 或 IP。

sentences.en: It doesn’t work the other way around; if an IETF standard doesn’t catch on with implementers and users, it gets ignored (and many have).
sentences.zh: 反之则不然。如果 IETF 标准没有受到实施者和用户的欢迎，它就会被忽视（许多人都被忽视）。

blocks.html_en: The Internet is for End Users argues that this soft power should be explicitly acknowledged, so that participants are more conscious of the real-world ramifications of their decisions.

sentences.en: The Internet is for End Users argues that this soft power should be explicitly acknowledged, so that participants are more conscious of the real-world ramifications of their decisions.
sentences.zh: 互联网是为最终用户服务的，认为这种软实力应该得到明确承认，以便参与者更加意识到他们的决定对现实世界的影响。

blocks.html_en: DNS over HTTPS is an interesting case study. It got the IETF mentioned in the UK Parliament by Baroness Thornton, a child safety advocate concerned about DoH’s use to bypass DNS-based controls mandated by UK law:

sentences.en: DNS over HTTPS is an interesting case study.
sentences.zh: DNS over HTTPS 是一个有趣的案例研究。

sentences.en: It got the IETF mentioned in the UK Parliament by Baroness Thornton, a child safety advocate concerned about DoH’s use to bypass DNS-based controls mandated by UK law:
sentences.zh: 儿童安全倡导者桑顿男爵夫人 (Baroness Thornton) 在英国议会中提到了 IETF，她对卫生部使用绕过英国法律规定的基于 DNS 的控制措施表示担忧：

blocks.html_en: ’[T]here is a fundamental and very concerning lack of accountability when obscure technical groups, peopled largely by the employees of the big internet companies, take decisions that have major public policy implications with enormous consequences for all of us…’

sentences.en: ’[T]here is a fundamental and very concerning lack of accountability when obscure technical groups, peopled largely by the employees of the big internet companies, take decisions that have major public policy implications with enormous consequences for all of us…’
sentences.zh: “当主要由大型互联网公司员工组成的默默无闻的技术团体做出对我们所有人产生重大影响的重大公共政策影响的决策时，就存在一种根本性的、非常令人担忧的问责制缺失……”

blocks.html_en: ’[T]here is a fundamental and very concerning lack of accountability when obscure technical groups, peopled largely by the employees of the big internet companies, take decisions that have major public policy implications with enormous consequences for all of us…’

sentences.en: ’[T]here is a fundamental and very concerning lack of accountability when obscure technical groups, peopled largely by the employees of the big internet companies, take decisions that have major public policy implications with enormous consequences for all of us…’
sentences.zh: “当主要由大型互联网公司员工组成的默默无闻的技术团体做出对我们所有人产生重大影响的重大公共政策影响的决策时，就存在一种根本性的、非常令人担忧的问责制缺失……”

blocks.html_en: However, DoH was designed, contributed and ultimately deployed by participants from Web browsers, not the IETF, who cannot stop vendors from deploying a protocol it doesn’t approve of (as is often said, ‘there are no standards police.’). The IETF’s contribution was putting the specification through its process to assess its technical suitability and adherence to established principles.

sentences.en: However, DoH was designed, contributed and ultimately deployed by participants from Web browsers, not the IETF, who cannot stop vendors from deploying a protocol it doesn’t approve of (as is often said, ‘there are no standards police.’).
sentences.zh: 然而，DoH 是由 Web 浏览器的参与者设计、贡献和最终部署的，而不是 IETF，IETF 无法阻止供应商部署它不认可的协议（正如人们常说的，“没有标准警察”）。

sentences.en: The IETF’s contribution was putting the specification through its process to assess its technical suitability and adherence to established principles.
sentences.zh: IETF 的贡献是通过其流程来评估该规范的技术适用性以及对既定原则的遵守情况。

blocks.html_en: Did the IETF create a better internet when it approved DoH? There’s a lot of disagreement about that, but what has upset many is that DoH was a surprise — the IETF standardised it without consulting some who it was likely to affect. Here, the IETF could have done better. The Internet is for End Users argues that such consultation is important, to assure that the people writing and reviewing the protocols understand how they will be used, and how they will impact users.

sentences.en: Did the IETF create a better internet when it approved DoH?
sentences.zh: IETF 批准 DoH 后是否创造了更好的互联网？

sentences.en: There’s a lot of disagreement about that, but what has upset many is that DoH was a surprise — the IETF standardised it without consulting some who it was likely to affect.
sentences.zh: 对此存在很多分歧，但让许多人感到不安的是，DoH 出人意料——IETF 在没有咨询可能影响的人的情况下就对其进行了标准化。

sentences.en: Here, the IETF could have done better.
sentences.zh: 在这方面，IETF 可以做得更好。

sentences.en: The Internet is for End Users argues that such consultation is important, to assure that the people writing and reviewing the protocols understand how they will be used, and how they will impact users.
sentences.zh: 互联网是为最终用户服务的，认为这种协商很重要，以确保编写和审查协议的人员了解它们将如何使用，以及它们将如何影响用户。

blocks.html_en: In the case of DoH, better communication between the technical community (not just big tech companies) and policymakers would clarified that relying on DNS to impose filtering was a bad assumption, in light of the principles underlying the design of the Internet.

sentences.en: In the case of DoH, better communication between the technical community (not just big tech companies) and policymakers would clarified that relying on DNS to impose filtering was a bad assumption, in light of the principles underlying the design of the Internet.
sentences.zh: 就卫生部而言，技术界（不仅仅是大型科技公司）和政策制定者之间更好的沟通将澄清，鉴于互联网设计的基本原则，依靠 DNS 实施过滤是一个糟糕的假设。

blocks.html_en:
“From its inception, the Internet has been, and is expected to remain, an evolving system whose participants regularly factor new requirements and technology into its design and implementation. Users of the Internet and providers of the equipment, software, and services that support it should anticipate and embrace this evolution as a major tenet of Internet philosophy.”
— The Internet Standards Process

sentences.en: “From its inception, the Internet has been, and is expected to remain, an evolving system whose participants regularly factor new requirements and technology into its design and implementation.
sentences.zh: “从诞生之日起，互联网一直是并且预计将继续是一个不断发展的系统，其参与者定期将新的要求和技术纳入其设计和实施中。

sentences.en: Users of the Internet and providers of the equipment, software, and services that support it should anticipate and embrace this evolution as a major tenet of Internet philosophy.” — The Internet Standards Process
sentences.zh: 互联网用户以及支持互联网的设备、软件和服务的提供商应该预见并接受这种演变，将其作为互联网哲学的主要原则。” — 互联网标准流程

blocks.html_en: However, that consultation does not translate to giving other parties a veto over Internet protocols. The UK Government or any other external authority should not be able to stop the IETF from creating a particular standard, or to hold it directly accountable; that would be a radical break from how the Internet has been developed for over thirty years. Because of the global nature of the Internet, it wouldn’t be possible to pursue a bilateral or regional style of governance; decisions would have to be sanctioned by every government where the Internet operates. That’s difficult to achieve even for vague statements of shared goals; doing it for the details of network protocols is impractical.

sentences.en: However, that consultation does not translate to giving other parties a veto over Internet protocols.
sentences.zh: 然而，这种协商并不意味着给予其他各方对互联网协议的否决权。

sentences.en: The UK Government or any other external authority should not be able to stop the IETF from creating a particular standard, or to hold it directly accountable; that would be a radical break from how the Internet has been developed for over thirty years.
sentences.zh: 英国政府或任何其他外部机构不应能够阻止 IETF 创建特定标准，或追究其直接责任；这将彻底打破互联网三十多年来的发展方式。

sentences.en: Because of the global nature of the Internet, it wouldn’t be possible to pursue a bilateral or regional style of governance; decisions would have to be sanctioned by every government where the Internet operates.
sentences.zh: 由于互联网的全球性，不可能追求双边或区域的治理方式；决策必须得到互联网运营地每个政府的批准。

sentences.en: That’s difficult to achieve even for vague statements of shared goals; doing it for the details of network protocols is impractical.
sentences.zh: 即使对于共同目标的模糊表述也很难实现；为了网络协议的细节而这样做是不切实际的。

blocks.html_en: Who, then, is the IETF accountable to? Besides the internal rules which assure that the standards process runs in a way that’s accountable to the technical community, ultimately the IETF is accountable to the Internet; if it strays too far from what vendors, networks, users, and governments want to do, it will lose relevance. As with any platform, the Internet is a beneficiary of the network effect, and if the IETF leads it in a direction that’s unacceptable in too many places, the Internet might fragment into several networks — a risk currently on many people’s minds.

sentences.en: Who, then, is the IETF accountable to?
sentences.zh: 那么，IETF 对谁负责呢？

sentences.en: Besides the internal rules which assure that the standards process runs in a way that’s accountable to the technical community, ultimately the IETF is accountable to the Internet; if it strays too far from what vendors, networks, users, and governments want to do, it will lose relevance.
sentences.zh: 除了确保标准流程以对技术社区负责的方式运行的内部规则外，IETF 最终还要对互联网负责；如果它与供应商、网络、用户和政府想要做的事情相差太远，它将失去相关性。

sentences.en: As with any platform, the Internet is a beneficiary of the network effect, and if the IETF leads it in a direction that’s unacceptable in too many places, the Internet might fragment into several networks — a risk currently on many people’s minds.
sentences.zh: 与任何平台一样，互联网是网络效应的受益者，如果 IETF 将其引向在太多地方不可接受的方向，互联网可能会分裂成多个网络——这是目前许多人心目中的风险。

blocks.html_en: Finding what’s best for end users

sentences.en: Finding what’s best for end users
sentences.zh: 寻找最适合最终用户的东西

blocks.html_en: There are also bound to be situations where what is best for end users is not obvious. Some will claim that giving other parties power — to filter, to monitor, to block — is in the interest of end users. How will the IETF make those decisions?

sentences.en: There are also bound to be situations where what is best for end users is not obvious.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，对于最终用户来说什么是最好的并不明显。

sentences.en: Some will claim that giving other parties power — to filter, to monitor, to block — is in the interest of end users.
sentences.zh: 有些人会声称，给予其他方权力——过滤、监控、阻止——符合最终用户的利益。

sentences.en: How will the IETF make those decisions?
sentences.zh: IETF 将如何做出这些决定？

blocks.html_en: Unsurprisingly, this has already happened; it refused to standardise wiretapping technology, for example. In doing so, it applied technical reasoning informed by principles and the global nature of the Internet; designing Internet standards to suit the laws of one or a few countries isn’t appropriate.

sentences.en: Unsurprisingly, this has already happened; it refused to standardise wiretapping technology, for example.
sentences.zh: 毫不奇怪，这已经发生了；例如，它拒绝标准化窃听技术。

sentences.en: In doing so, it applied technical reasoning informed by principles and the global nature of the Internet; designing Internet standards to suit the laws of one or a few countries isn’t appropriate.
sentences.zh: 在此过程中，它应用了基于互联网原理和全球性质的技术推理；设计互联网标准来适应一个或几个国家的法律是不合适的。

blocks.html_en: That is echoed by The Internet is for End Users, which says:

sentences.en: That is echoed by The Internet is for End Users, which says:
sentences.zh: 《互联网是为最终用户服务的》呼应了这一点，其中说：

blocks.html_en: [W]hen a decision improves the Internet for end users in one jurisdiction, but at the cost of potential harm to others elsewhere, that is not a good tradeoff. As such, we effectively design the Internet for the pessimal environment.

sentences.en: [W]hen a decision improves the Internet for end users in one jurisdiction, but at the cost of potential harm to others elsewhere, that is not a good tradeoff.
sentences.zh: 当一项决定改善一个司法管辖区的最终用户的互联网时，但代价是对其他地方的其他人造成潜在的伤害，这不是一个好的权衡。

sentences.en: As such, we effectively design the Internet for the pessimal environment.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们有效地为悲观环境设计了互联网。

blocks.html_en: [W]hen a decision improves the Internet for end users in one jurisdiction, but at the cost of potential harm to others elsewhere, that is not a good tradeoff. As such, we effectively design the Internet for the pessimal environment.

sentences.en: [W]hen a decision improves the Internet for end users in one jurisdiction, but at the cost of potential harm to others elsewhere, that is not a good tradeoff.
sentences.zh: 当一项决定改善一个司法管辖区的最终用户的互联网时，但代价是对其他地方的其他人造成潜在的伤害，这不是一个好的权衡。

sentences.en: As such, we effectively design the Internet for the pessimal environment.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们有效地为悲观环境设计了互联网。

blocks.html_en: Even with careful thought, technical acumen and broad consultation, the IETF is bound to get some decisions wrong. That’s OK. RFC stands for Request for Comments, and in that spirit, sometimes the comments — evidenced by adoption and deployment as well — tell us to revise our specifications. That spirit of humility is still very much alive in the IETF community.

sentences.en: Even with careful thought, technical acumen and broad consultation, the IETF is bound to get some decisions wrong.
sentences.zh: 即使经过缜密的思考、技术敏锐性和广泛的咨询，IETF 也难免会做出一些错误的决定。

sentences.en: That’s OK.
sentences.zh: 没关系。

sentences.en: RFC stands for Request for Comments, and in that spirit, sometimes the comments — evidenced by adoption and deployment as well — tell us to revise our specifications.
sentences.zh: RFC 代表请求评论，本着这种精神，有时评论（也通过采用和部署证明）告诉我们修改我们的规范。

sentences.en: That spirit of humility is still very much alive in the IETF community.
sentences.zh: 这种谦逊的精神在 IETF 社区中仍然非常活跃。

blocks.html_en: Next steps

sentences.en: Next steps
sentences.zh: 后续步骤

blocks.html_en: The Internet has been with us for almost 40 years and has contributed to profound changes in society. It currently faces serious challenges — issues that require input from policymakers, civil society, ordinary citizens, businesses and technologists.

sentences.en: The Internet has been with us for almost 40 years and has contributed to profound changes in society.
sentences.zh: 互联网已经陪伴我们近 40 年，为社会带来了深刻的变化。

sentences.en: It currently faces serious challenges — issues that require input from policymakers, civil society, ordinary citizens, businesses and technologists.
sentences.zh: 它目前面临着严峻的挑战——需要政策制定者、民间社会、普通公民、企业和技术专家的投入。

blocks.html_en: It’s past time for technologists to both become more involved in discussions about how to meet those challenges, and to consider broader views of how the technology they create fits into society. Without good communication, policymakers are prone to making rules that doesn’t work with the technology, and technologists are prone to creating technology naïve to its policy implications.

sentences.en: It’s past time for technologists to both become more involved in discussions about how to meet those challenges, and to consider broader views of how the technology they create fits into society.
sentences.zh: 技术专家现在应该更多地参与如何应对这些挑战的讨论，并考虑他们创造的技术如何融入社会的更广泛的观点。

sentences.en: Without good communication, policymakers are prone to making rules that doesn’t work with the technology, and technologists are prone to creating technology naïve to its policy implications.
sentences.zh: 如果没有良好的沟通，政策制定者很容易制定不适合技术的规则，而技术专家则很容易创建对其政策影响不了解的技术。

blocks.html_en: So at its heart, The Internet is for End Users is a call for IETF participants to stop pretending that they can ignore the non-technical consequences of their decisions, a call for broader consultation when making them, and one for continued focus on the end user. Ultimately, end user impact is as least as important as the technical considerations of a proposal, and judging that impact requires a more serious effort to understand and incorporate other non-technical views.

sentences.en: So at its heart, The Internet is for End Users is a call for IETF participants to stop pretending that they can ignore the non-technical consequences of their decisions, a call for broader consultation when making them, and one for continued focus on the end user.
sentences.zh: 因此，从本质上讲，《互联网是为了最终用户》呼吁 IETF 参与者停止假装他们可以忽略其决策的非技术后果，呼吁在制定决策时进行更广泛的协商，并呼吁继续关注最终用户。

sentences.en: Ultimately, end user impact is as least as important as the technical considerations of a proposal, and judging that impact requires a more serious effort to understand and incorporate other non-technical views.
sentences.zh: 最终，最终用户的影响与提案的技术考虑因素一样重要，而判断这种影响需要更认真的努力来理解和纳入其他非技术观点。

blocks.html_en: The Internet is for End Users is an IAB document; it doesn't have IETF consensus. As such, it doesn’t bind IETF decisions, but it is considered persuasive because the IAB has a mandate to consider issues affecting the Internet architecture.

sentences.en: The Internet is for End Users is an IAB document; it doesn't have IETF consensus.
sentences.zh: Internet is for End Users 是一份 IAB 文件；它没有 IETF 共识。

sentences.en: As such, it doesn’t bind IETF decisions, but it is considered persuasive because the IAB has a mandate to consider issues affecting the Internet architecture.
sentences.zh: 因此，它并不约束 IETF 的决策，但它被认为具有说服力，因为 IAB 有权考虑影响互联网架构的问题。

blocks.html_en: On its own, then, it has limited effect. I view it as a small contribution to a larger body of principled thought that can help inform decisions about the evolution of the Internet. It’s up to all of us to apply those principles and develop them further.

sentences.en: On its own, then, it has limited effect.
sentences.zh: 那么，它本身的作用是有限的。

sentences.en: I view it as a small contribution to a larger body of principled thought that can help inform decisions about the evolution of the Internet.
sentences.zh: 我认为它是对更大的原则性思想的一个小小的贡献，可以帮助为有关互联网发展的决策提供信息。

sentences.en: It’s up to all of us to apply those principles and develop them further.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都有责任应用这些原则并进一步发展它们。

content_html_zh:
星期五, 28 八月 2020

标准

互联网架构委员会 (IAB) 发布了 RFC8890，互联网是为最终用户服务的，认为互联网工程任务组 (IETF) 的决策应基于对互联网用户有利的原则，并且应采取积极措施来实现这一目标。

为什么需要这么说呢？ 是不是太过分了？ 他们还能支持谁，你为什么要关心？ 作为 RFC 的作者和通过该 RFC 的 IAB 成员，以下是我的想法。

互联网是如何形成的

IETF 在互联网的设计和运营中发挥着核心作用。 它由创建了多项互联网核心技术的工程师于 20 世纪 80 年代成立，是记录互联网技术设计的主要场所，并监督 TCP、IP、DNS 和 HTTP 等协议的开发。

公司、政府和其他组织并未正式参与 IETF；人们只代表他们自己。 甚至没有会员资格的概念。 相反，有关规范的决定是通过“粗略共识”做出的——IETF 试图根据提出的想法、评论和担忧找到每个问题的最佳解决方案，而不是正式投票。

“最好”并不意味着得到最多公司支持的选择；它背后有最好的技术论证。 工作组主席衡量这一共识；如果有人认为自己错了，他们可以通过一系列根据他们的经验选择的权威机构提出上诉。

或者，用非官方 IETF 信条的话来说：“我们拒绝国王、总统和投票。” 我们相信粗略的共识和运行代码。”

技术还是政治？ 两个都

当然，大多数 IETF 决策都是关于技术细节的；哪些字节应该放在哪里，服务器如何对客户端做出反应，等等。 正因为如此，参与者经常告诉自己，他们的决定从来都不是政治性的；他们的决定与政治无关。任何此类问题都发生在“第 8 层”上——指的是网络协议常用的七个抽象堆栈——因此无需担心。

“运行由我们的流程产生的代码（当事情运行良好时）不可避免地会产生超出技术考虑的影响，因为基本决策提供了一些用途，同时阻碍了其他用途。” — 互联网是为最终用户服务的

然而，就像大多数抽象概念一样，网络上的比特和政治事务之间的障碍已经被证明是有漏洞的。 有时，发送信息（或阻止信息）的能力会产生现实世界的后果，即夺取某些人的权力并将其交给其他人。 同样，能够看到其他人在说什么，并控制他们说话的格式。

因此，在一个与互联网日益交织在一起的世界中，维持互联网协议的设计不具有政治维度的立场变得越来越困难。 所有的决定都可能存在偏见；对不同各方有利或不利的情况。

例如，最近的 DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) 标准化让持不同政见者和抗议者的拥护者与使用 DNS 进行集中式网络管理的网络运营商以及推广基于 DNS 的过滤解决方案的儿童安全倡导者展开了对立。 如果 IETF 仅根据技术优点做出决定，它将如何平衡这些利益？

另一个例子是 Encrypted Client Hello 提案，它弥补了与任何监听者共享您访问的 HTTPS 站点身份的漏洞。 据报道，中国已开始阻止使用它的连接，因此从纯粹的技术意义上来说，它不会很好地工作，因为某些网络会阻止它。 IETF 应该停止这方面的工作吗？

另一个例子：IETF 应如何处理允许网络解密或中间 HTTPS 连接的提案？ 如果仅仅是技术上合理的话可以吗？ 如果用户同意怎么办？“同意”是什么意思？ 已经提出了许多这样的建议，但没有获得批准。 为什么？

如果 IETF 的决定影响互联网的设计，而互联网是政治性的，那么 IETF 的决定有时也是政治性的。 然而，其决策过程假定每个问题都有技术上正确的答案。 当这个决定影响现实世界中的人和权力时，粗略的共识和运行代码是不够的。

多年来，这些问题变得越来越紧迫，因为做出具有政治结果的决策但仅使用技术论证来解释它们是不可行的。 这危及了 IETF 决策的合法性，因为这些决策可能被视为任意的，尤其是对于那些失败的一方。

许多规则制定系统——无论是法院、立法机构还是标准机构——通过采取有原则的方法来建立合法性。 同意基于共同价值观的原则的社区可以利用这些原则来做出艰难的决策。 因此，考虑 IETF 用来指导互联网发展的原则是合理的。

互联网的原理

我们所知道的互联网是它成长的时代的产物。 法治和平等、理性、自由、权利和财产等自由主义价值观在战后美国和欧洲的政治格局中占据主导地位，而最早期的互联网发展就发生在这些地方。

“IETF 社区希望互联网取得成功，因为我们相信互联网的存在及其对经济、通信和教育的影响将帮助我们建设一个更美好的人类社会。” — IETF 的使命宣言

互联网已经隐含地嵌入了这些价值观。 您不需要许可证（甚至不需要披露您的身份）即可使用它，并且其技术基础使得很难强制执行该要求。 任何人都可以发表文章，因此政府需要付出巨大的努力来限制言论和自由集会的权利——这在一定程度上也是由于它的设计方式。 没有任何中央机构来决定哪些网络可以或不能连接到互联网。 您无需事先获得许可即可创建新的 Internet 应用程序（就像蒂姆·伯纳斯·李很久以前创建 Web 时所做的那样）。 这种开放性常常被认为对互联网的成功至关重要。

然而，随着新人参与工作并面临新挑战，隐含的价值观可能会发生变化。 当最终的决策对利润和社会产生深远影响时尤其如此。 因此，多年来，IETF 社区在记录可指导决策的明确原则方面取得了进展。

例如，RFC 7258 普遍监控是一种攻击建立了 IETF 共识，即允许广泛、隐蔽的监控对互联网不利，因此 IETF 将设计其协议来减轻这种风险——这是一个具有政治动机和后果的技术论点。

同样，RFC 6973 记录了互联网协议的隐私注意事项，RFC 8752 报告了 IAB 研讨会，该研讨会探讨了新闻出版商与大型在线平台之间的权力动态。

或者，考虑端到端原则，该原则规定应用程序的功能应驻留在终端节点（例如，您的计算机或电话）而不是网络中。

IETF 社区将（我希望）继续以共同价值观为基础记录和探索这些原则。 RFC8890 对此做出了小小的贡献，要求 IETF 社区在发生冲突时支持互联网的最终用户（换句话说，实际的人），而不是要求满足其需求的其他利益相关者。

我们不能只拘泥于技术

如果 IETF 没有任何基本原则，它就会只关注技术。 互联网是为最终用户服务的一些批评者表示，这正是它应该做的。 这意味着只要技术上足够，它就会发布任何提案，无论其效果如何。

一些标准机构已经以这种方式运作；只要你能让几个人（或更常见的是公司）聚集在一起并就某件事达成一致，你就可以将其发布。 IETF 没有；它经常拒绝采纳建议。

“当 IETF 拥有某个协议或功能时，它就对该协议的所有方面承担责任，即使某些方面可能很少或永远不会在互联网上看到。” — IETF 的使命宣言

这种拒绝的能力对于组织内外的许多人来说都是有意义的。 IETF 标准化某些东西意味着它对互联网有利，并且不仅对技术适用性进行了审查，而且还对互联网设计原则的遵守进行了审查。 换句话说，IETF 是一个质量过滤器；如果某个规范在那里达成共识，它就会得到更广泛、更容易的部署（尽管无论如何这并不能保证成功），因为人们知道它已经过审查。

仅仅为了避免思考和应用原则而放弃这一角色对于互联网来说并不好。 虽然它可能会赢得一些渴望利用的参与者，但它也会失去很多人——包括许多仍然投资于互联网作为世界正义力量的人。

在许多人看来，这样做还会影响 IETF 在互联网治理中的作用的合法性。 科学家和工程师长期以来一直关注他们的工作如何影响世界及其被滥用的可能性。 IETF 延续了这一传统，并且应该公开这样做。

熟悉 IETF 的力量

如果 IETF 是根据它认为对用户有利的方式做出决策，那么它是否会将自己定位为某种管理机构，从而从政府和其他机构手中夺取权力？ 把如此重要的事情交给那些出现的、没有任何民主合法性的极客手中，不是很危险吗？

首先，现实检查。 IETF 的决定仅与文件有关；他们不控制互联网。 设备和软件供应商、最终用户、平台和网络运营商以及最终政府等其他各方对于互联网上每天实际发生的事情拥有更多发言权。

IETF 拥有设计大规模协议的能力、引导提案与其原则保持一致的能力，以及赋予其文档一定严肃性的声誉。 这些吸引了这些各方加入 IETF 作为标准化场所，他们的力量流向了它所认可的规范——尤其是当协议具有势头时，例如 HTTP 或 IP。 反之则不然。如果 IETF 标准没有受到实施者和用户的欢迎，它就会被忽视（许多人都被忽视）。

互联网是为最终用户服务的，认为这种软实力应该得到明确承认，以便参与者更加意识到他们的决定对现实世界的影响。

DNS over HTTPS 是一个有趣的案例研究。 儿童安全倡导者桑顿男爵夫人 (Baroness Thornton) 在英国议会中提到了 IETF，她对卫生部使用绕过英国法律规定的基于 DNS 的控制措施表示担忧：

“当主要由大型互联网公司员工组成的默默无闻的技术团体做出对我们所有人产生重大影响的重大公共政策影响的决策时，就存在一种根本性的、非常令人担忧的问责制缺失……”

然而，DoH 是由 Web 浏览器的参与者设计、贡献和最终部署的，而不是 IETF，IETF 无法阻止供应商部署它不认可的协议（正如人们常说的，“没有标准警察”）。 IETF 的贡献是通过其流程来评估该规范的技术适用性以及对既定原则的遵守情况。

IETF 批准 DoH 后是否创造了更好的互联网？ 对此存在很多分歧，但让许多人感到不安的是，DoH 出人意料——IETF 在没有咨询可能影响的人的情况下就对其进行了标准化。 在这方面，IETF 可以做得更好。 互联网是为最终用户服务的，认为这种协商很重要，以确保编写和审查协议的人员了解它们将如何使用，以及它们将如何影响用户。

就卫生部而言，技术界（不仅仅是大型科技公司）和政策制定者之间更好的沟通将澄清，鉴于互联网设计的基本原则，依靠 DNS 实施过滤是一个糟糕的假设。

“从诞生之日起，互联网一直是并且预计将继续是一个不断发展的系统，其参与者定期将新的要求和技术纳入其设计和实施中。 互联网用户以及支持互联网的设备、软件和服务的提供商应该预见并接受这种演变，将其作为互联网哲学的主要原则。” — 互联网标准流程

然而，这种协商并不意味着给予其他各方对互联网协议的否决权。 英国政府或任何其他外部机构不应能够阻止 IETF 创建特定标准，或追究其直接责任；这将彻底打破互联网三十多年来的发展方式。 由于互联网的全球性，不可能追求双边或区域的治理方式；决策必须得到互联网运营地每个政府的批准。 即使对于共同目标的模糊表述也很难实现；为了网络协议的细节而这样做是不切实际的。

那么，IETF 对谁负责呢？ 除了确保标准流程以对技术社区负责的方式运行的内部规则外，IETF 最终还要对互联网负责；如果它与供应商、网络、用户和政府想要做的事情相差太远，它将失去相关性。 与任何平台一样，互联网是网络效应的受益者，如果 IETF 将其引向在太多地方不可接受的方向，互联网可能会分裂成多个网络——这是目前许多人心目中的风险。

寻找最适合最终用户的东西

在某些情况下，对于最终用户来说什么是最好的并不明显。 有些人会声称，给予其他方权力——过滤、监控、阻止——符合最终用户的利益。 IETF 将如何做出这些决定？

毫不奇怪，这已经发生了；例如，它拒绝标准化窃听技术。 在此过程中，它应用了基于互联网原理和全球性质的技术推理；设计互联网标准来适应一个或几个国家的法律是不合适的。

《互联网是为最终用户服务的》呼应了这一点，其中说：

当一项决定改善一个司法管辖区的最终用户的互联网时，但代价是对其他地方的其他人造成潜在的伤害，这不是一个好的权衡。 因此，我们有效地为悲观环境设计了互联网。

即使经过缜密的思考、技术敏锐性和广泛的咨询，IETF 也难免会做出一些错误的决定。 没关系。 RFC 代表请求评论，本着这种精神，有时评论（也通过采用和部署证明）告诉我们修改我们的规范。 这种谦逊的精神在 IETF 社区中仍然非常活跃。

后续步骤

互联网已经陪伴我们近 40 年，为社会带来了深刻的变化。 它目前面临着严峻的挑战——需要政策制定者、民间社会、普通公民、企业和技术专家的投入。

技术专家现在应该更多地参与如何应对这些挑战的讨论，并考虑他们创造的技术如何融入社会的更广泛的观点。 如果没有良好的沟通，政策制定者很容易制定不适合技术的规则，而技术专家则很容易创建对其政策影响不了解的技术。

因此，从本质上讲，《互联网是为了最终用户》呼吁 IETF 参与者停止假装他们可以忽略其决策的非技术后果，呼吁在制定决策时进行更广泛的协商，并呼吁继续关注最终用户。 最终，最终用户的影响与提案的技术考虑因素一样重要，而判断这种影响需要更认真的努力来理解和纳入其他非技术观点。

Internet is for End Users 是一份 IAB 文件；它没有 IETF 共识。 因此，它并不约束 IETF 的决策，但它被认为具有说服力，因为 IAB 有权考虑影响互联网架构的问题。

那么，它本身的作用是有限的。 我认为它是对更大的原则性思想的一个小小的贡献，可以帮助为有关互联网发展的决策提供信息。 我们所有人都有责任应用这些原则并进一步发展它们。
